October 23, 1941.

Shanghai City Government - Bureau of
Finance establishes Land Tax Collection
Office in Western District, O C.L.

The Bureau of Finance of the Shanghai City
Government recently established a land tax collection
office (上海市財政局年租征收處 ) at 9-A Tifeng Road
with Mr. CHEN SUNG ( 陳 森 ) in charge. The tax
is to be known as the "permanent land lease tax"
(永租契地年租) and will be collected in the
Chinese territory and the extra-Settlement roads area
adjacent to the International Settlement and the
French Concession. A tax of $1.40 per mow will be
levied in the Shanghai area and $2.00 per mow in the
Paoshan area. The collection will be made according
to the documents previously in possession of the
Land and Finance Bureaux of the former Shanghai City
Government.

As far as is known, the new collection office
has not yet formally started functioning. There is no
signboard outside the office.

1941年10月23日。

上海市政府财政局在越界筑路区（O.C.L.）西区设立土地税征收处

上海市政府财政局最近在提丰路9-A号设立了一个土地税征收处（上海市財政局年租征收處），由陈森（CHEN SUNG）先生负责。该税种称为“永租契地年租”，将在华界以及毗邻国际租界和法租界的越界筑路区域征收。上海地区每亩征收1.40元，宝山地区每亩征收2.00元。征税将依据前上海市政府土地局和财政局此前持有的文件进行。

据所知，新的征收处尚未正式运作。办公室外没有挂牌。

February 7, 1941.

Western District Branch Office of the Finance Bureau
of the Shanghai City Government - activities.
------------------

The Western District Branch of the Finance
Bureau of the Shanghai City Government, 92 Jessfield
Road, has decided to increase the municipal tax with
effect from January 1, 1941 at the following rates :-

| | Old Rate | New Rate |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Residence | 9% | 12% |
| Shop and factories | 11% | 14% |

The Branch in question is collecting the municipal tax
for the winter quarter, 1940 in the area under its
jurisdiction, and will make re-assessment when levy
is made according to the new rate.

The business tax so far remains unchanged,
i.e. 0.3% to 0.5% from factories and 0.1½% to 0.3%
from shops, but it is learned that the tax will be
also increased at a rate to be announced later.

上海市政府财政局西区办事处 - 活动。
---

上海市政府财政局西区办事处（极司菲尔路92号）决定自1941年1月1日起提高市政税，税率如下：-

| | 旧税率 | 新税率 |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| 住宅 | 9% | 12% |
| 商店和工厂 | 11% | 14% |

该办事处正在其管辖区域内征收1940年冬季季度的市政税，并在按新税率征收时进行重新评估。

营业税目前保持不变，即工厂为0.3%至0.5%，商店为0.1½%至0.3%，但据悉该税也将增加，具体税率待后公布。

page_data.en:
Western District Branch Office of the Finance Bureau
of the Shanghai City Government - activities.

On January 16, the Western District Branch Office
of the Finance Bureau of the Shanghai City Government, 92
Jessfield Road, commenced the collection of Municipal rates
for the Winter quarters, 1940 and of the Business Tax
for the second half year of 1940 in the area under its
jurisdiction. The Municipal rate is equivalent to 11%
of the house rentals, while the business tax ranges from
0.3% to 0.5% of the profits realized. It is said that
collections have already been carried out at a number of
commercial firms and residences in the extra-Settlement
roads area and was carried out when the former chief
CHU TSENG (朱真), was in charge of the office, but
details are not available regarding the places. Some
forty members have now been despatched by the new chief
BEI YU MING (裴玉鳴) to conduct investigations into
the residents and collect the taxes.
page_data.zh:
上海市政府财政局西区办事处 - 活动。

1月16日，上海市政府财政局西区办事处（极司菲尔路92号）开始在其管辖区域内征收1940年冬季季度的市政捐及1940年下半年的营业税。市政捐相当于房屋租金的11%，而营业税范围为实现利润的0.3%至0.5%。据说，在前任主管朱真（CHU TSENG）负责该办事处期间，已在越界筑路区域的一些商行和住宅进行了征收，但关于地点的详情不详。新任主管裴玉鸣（BEI YU MING）现已派遣约四十名成员调查居民并征收税款。

MUNICIPAL POLICE
D. 85-99 Y
January 14, 1941 / 41

Situation in the Western District

The situation in the Western District
remained unchanged this morning, January 14.
During the morning, it was observed that a Revenue-
collector from the Western District Branch of the
Bureau of Finance, Shanghai City Government, House 1,
92 Jessfield Road, accompanied by a S.C.G.P.B.
policeman was collecting taxes from the stall-
keepers in the vicinity of Brenan Piece, who number
approximately 800. The taxes are divided into
the following grades :-
1) "A" Class: $1.50 per month (for stalls
selling pork and fish etc.)
2) "B" Class: $1.00 per month (for big
vegetable stalls).
3. "C" Class: $0.50 per month (for small
vegetable stalls).

While collecting the taxes, the Revenue-collector,
is said to have informed the payers that the S.M.C.
authorities will no longer collect licence fees and
that the people concerned should refuse to make such
a payment if called upon to do so by the said
authorities.

It will be noted that before the removal of
the barbed wire entanglements in that area, the S.M.C.
were collecting licence fees of $2.40 per month from
each stall.

（印：INDEXED BY REGISTRY DATE 15/1 / 41）
page_data.zh:
工部局警务处
D. 85-99 Y
1941年1月14日 / 41

西区局势

1月14日上午，西区局势
保持不变。上午观察到，上海市政府
财政局西区办事处（极司菲尔路92号1室）的一名
收税员，由一名上海中国警察局的
警员陪同，正在布伦南片场（Brenan Piece）附近向大约
800名摊贩收税。税款分为
以下等级：-
1) “A”类：每月1.50元（用于出售
猪肉和鱼等的摊位）
2) “B”类：每月1.00元（用于大型
蔬菜摊位）。
3. “C”类：每月0.50元（用于小型
蔬菜摊位）。

据说在收税时，收税员告知
纳税人，工部局当局将不再收取执照费，
如果上述当局要求支付此类费用，
相关人员应拒绝支付。

值得注意的是，在该区域拆除铁丝网障碍之前，
工部局向每个摊位每月收取2.40元的执照费。

（印：档案室索引编制 日期 1941年1月15日）

January 3, 1941

WESTERN DISTRICT BRANCH OFFICE OF THE FINANCE
BUREAU OF THE SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT - ACTIVITIES.

Mr. Bei Yu Ming (北 玉 明) has been appointed
chief of the Western District Branch Office of the
Finance Bureau of the Shanghai City Government, 92
Jessfield Road, in succession to Mr. Chu Tseng (朱 真),
who relinquished his post on December 31, 1940 on orders
from Mayor Cheng Kung Poh. The new chief is a relative
of Mr. Chow Fuh Hai (周 佛 海), ex-Minister of Police
of the Nanking Government, now Managing-Director of the
new "Central Bank of China".

According to information obtained, the Eastern
District Branch of the Finance Bureau proposes to
collect the following taxes in the Western District,
O.O.L.:

| | Present rate. | Proposed rate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Municipal rates | 11% | 13% |
| Business tax | 0.3% - 0.5% | 0.8%- 1% |

Await Police Agreement
SMC Confirms
Parleys Loom
On Tax Muddle

A high official of the S.M.C.
Revenue Department, yesterday
confirmed the recent CHINA
PRESS report that negotiations
to settle the present tax mud-
dle in the western "outside
roads" area would be started
with the City Government of
Greater Shanghai as soon as the
signatures are put to the agree-
ment on the Special Outside
Roads Police Force.

The official made this statement
when approached by THE CHINA
PRESS on the report that the
West Shanghai Tax Collection
Bureau of the City Government
was demanding taxes from factories
within the 100-meter zone on both
sides of the outside roads. This
zone, according to the Land Regu-
lations, falls under the sole taxa-
tion of the S.M.C.

Tax collectors of the City Gov-
ernment have for many months
encroached on this sector, he said.
The official added that he did
not have sufficient information to
state that the practice was general,
but that specific cases had been
coming to his attention for a long
time.

Employees Said Kidnapped

This resulted in many ratepayers
in the "outside roads" area having
to pay both to the S.M.C. and the
City Government, he pointed out.
"We haven't lost much in taxes,"
he stated when asked whether the
S.M.C. had been excluded from the
sector by agents of the City Gov-
ernment. The latter, he said,
did not seem to object to rate-
payers paying taxes to the S.M.C.
so long as they paid their own ad-
ministration too.

Informed Chinese sources, mean-
while, said that the City Govern-
ment had from the very beginning
concentrated on collection of taxes
from factories within the 100-meter
zone. In some cases, when the
factories refused to accede to their
demands, they employed intimida-
tion methods, it was stated.

"Get What They Can"

One case was cited in which
the foreman of a factory was
reportedly kidnapped. The rest
of the workmen promptly re-
fused to return to work next
morning, also fearing reprisals.
In the end, these sources said,
the factory was forced to make
payment.

Many tax collectors of the City
Government "get what they can,
where they can," as they receive
commission on the sums they col-
lect, it was stated.

With probable tax negotiations
still awaiting signing of the "out-
side roads" police agreement, a
spokesman of the Municipal Police
revealed that the Settlement ad-
ministration was still waiting for
Mayor Chen Kung-po to make the
first move in the matter.
page_data.zh:
等待警方协议
工部局确认
谈判在即
关于税收混乱

工部局（S.M.C.）税务局的一名高级官员昨日证实了《字林西报》（CHINA PRESS）最近的报道，称一旦签署关于特别越界筑路区警队的协议，就将与大上海市政府开始谈判，以解决目前西部“越界筑路”地区的税收混乱局面。

当《字林西报》就市政府上海西区税务征收处要求越界筑路两侧100米区域内工厂缴纳税款的报道向该官员求证时，他发表了上述声明。根据《土地章程》，该区域属于工部局的独家征税范围。

他说，市政府的税务人员数月来一直侵入该区域。该官员补充说，他没有足够的信息表明这种做法是普遍的，但具体案例长期以来一直引起他的注意。

雇员被称遭绑架

他指出，这导致许多“越界筑路”地区的纳税人不得不既向工部局又向市政府缴纳税款。当被问及工部局是否已被市政府代理人排除在该区域之外时，他表示：“我们在税收方面损失不大。”他说，只要纳税人也向市政府行政机构缴税，后者似乎并不反对纳税人向工部局缴税。

与此同时，消息灵通的中方人士称，市政府从一开始就专注于征收越界筑路100米区域内工厂的税款。据说，在某些情况下，当工厂拒绝接受其要求时，他们采用了恐吓手段。

“能捞多少是多少”

有人举出一个案例，据说一家工厂的工头被绑架。其余工人因害怕遭到报复，第二天早上也拒绝复工。这些消息来源称，最终该工厂被迫付款。

据说，由于市政府的许多税务人员从其征收的金额中抽取佣金，因此他们“能在哪里捞就在哪里捞，能捞多少是多少”。

鉴于税收谈判可能仍有待签署“越界筑路”警察协议，一名工部局警务处发言人透露，租界当局仍在等待市长陈公博在此事上采取第一步行动。

National Herald, Chinese-American Daily News, Cheng Yien Pao,
Shun Pao, and Sin Wan Pao of December 26 :-

RATES IN THE OUTLYING ROADS AREA ILLEGALLY COLLECTED

It is rumoured that the so-called City
Government Western District Tax Collection Office has
written to the Chinese and foreign factories which are
within 100 metres from the two sides of the outlying roads
area of the Western District demanding a collection of taxes.
According to the Yangkingpang Land Regulations, the S.M.C.
own collect municipal rates from the districts within 100
metres of the outlying roads area.

Yesterday a reporter made a visit to the
S.M.C. Revenue Department asking about this matter. A
senior member of staff of that department told the reporter
that at the present time the municipal rate disputes could
not be settled, while negotiations could only be commenced
after the conclusion of an agreement on the joint Police
Force. A certain party has sent collectors on several
occasions to that district in an attempt to collect taxes.
Although the Revenue Department employee has secured no
detailed information, yet according to what he knows some
ratepayers, apart from paying municipal rates to the S.M.C.,
have also paid taxes to the certain party. As they are
willing to sustain loss, the Council cannot interfere with
them.

According to well-informed Chinese circles,
when some factories within 100 metres of the outlying roads
area refuse to pay taxes, the tax collectors of the certain
party sometimes have adopted threatening methods. It is
said that the tax collectors of the certain party have been
secretly instructed that if any taxes can be collected, they
can do what they like. With regard to the police agreement
on the outlying roads area, a spokesman of the S.M.P. said
that the authorities of the International Settlement are
waiting for the first movement of Chen Kung-po.

With reference to the establishment of the
Finance Bureau Western District Tax Collection Office
yesterday by the certain party, the reporter made a visit
to a senior member of staff of a certain factory in that
district asking him about the forcible collection of taxes.
He said that although the factory has received this kind of
notice, yet it has not yet decided how to deal with the matter.
This matter involved the financial affairs of the S.M.C. It
is expected that the S.M.C. finance authorities will adopt
ways and means in order to protect the original rights and
interests. Thus, the factory will decide to adopt measures
following the attitude of the S.M.C. With regard to the
question of taking out licences for different vehicles,
ricshas have been unable to proceed into the outlying roads
area if without "licences," while motor cars, bicycles, etc.
bearing the Settlement licences can go freely in the district.

12月26日的《国民新闻》、《中美日报》、《诚言报》、《申报》和《新晚报》：-

非法征收越界筑路区的捐税

谣传所谓市政府西区税务征收处已致函位于西区越界筑路区两侧100米内的中外工厂，要求征收税款。根据杨泾浜《土地章程》，工部局独自征收越界筑路区100米内区域的市政捐。

昨日，一名记者走访了工部局税务局询问此事。该局一名高级职员告诉记者，目前市政捐纠纷无法解决，只有在联合警队协议达成后才能开始谈判。某一方已多次派遣收税员前往该地区试图征税。虽然税务局职员没有掌握详细信息，但据他所知，一些纳税人除了向工部局缴纳市政捐外，还向某一方缴纳税款。由于他们愿意承受损失，工部局无法干预他们。

据消息灵通的中方圈子称，当越界筑路区100米内的一些工厂拒绝缴纳税款时，某一方的税务人员有时会采取威胁手段。据说，某一方的税务人员接到秘密指示，只要能征收到税款，他们可以随心所欲。关于越界筑路区的警察协议，工部局警务处（S.M.P.）发言人表示，国际租界当局正在等待陈公博的第一次举动。

关于某一方昨日设立财政局西区税务征收处一事，记者走访了该地区某工厂的一名高级职员，询问强制征税的情况。他说，虽然工厂收到了此类通知，但尚未决定如何处理此事。此事涉及工部局的财政事务。预计工部局财政当局将采取措施以保护原有权益。因此，工厂将根据工部局的态度决定采取相应措施。关于各类车辆领取执照的问题，如果没有“执照”，人力车无法进入越界筑路区，而悬挂租界执照的汽车、自行车等则可以在该地区自由通行。

West Area
Factories
Await Tax

Notice Sent By Finance
Bureau Asks Tax Fees
Payment In 3 Days

Though notifications were reported to have been sent out of the Western District Office of the Shanghai City Government Bureau of Finance to all industrial companies in the Western Area informing them that all premises within Chinese territory are subject to taxation by the City Government, no other direct steps have been taken, it was learnt yesterday.

The tax reminder was sent to both Chinese and foreign firms and reportedly read as follows: "You are hereby reminded that the location of your factory is inside Chinese territory. According to reports compiled by our officers your tax payments to the Shanghai Municipal Council every season are roughly estimated at the following figure. Kindly note that within three days of receipt of this notification you are cordially requested to deliver the various taxes dues from you for the various seasons to the Western District Office of the Finance Bureau of the City Government of Greater Shanghai at House 1, Lane 32, Jessfield Road. 21st day of the 12th Moon of the 29th year of the Republic of China."

All of the establishments receiving the above notification, informed circles stated yesterday, were located inside Chinese territory off the extra-Settlement Roads in the Western District, and in some cases when foreigners were concerned complaints were reported to have been made to the Bubbling Well Police Station.

by an armed uniformed member of the S.C.G.P.B., were on the

learning that, the collector was one named Zung Ong Jung
(陳鴻順), attached to the Western Branch Tax Office of
the Shanghai City Government Bureau of Finance, 92/1 Jes-
field Road.

of the business undertaken by the above plant, stated that,
the Business Tax was only levied on silk weaving filatures,

Subject (in full) Visit by official of the Finance Bureau, __________ to the
Associated American Industries factory, No. 7 Amherst Avenue.

Made by Inspector __________ Forwarded by J. M. Farlane C.I.

Sir,

I beg to report that at about 11.55 a.m. today,
a foreman of the above company telephoned Well Station
and reported that an official of the S.M.C. Finance Bureau,
accompanied by a S.M.C. policeman was trying to enter the
factory.

The undersigned, accompanied by C.I. Shin immediately
proceeded to No. 7 Amherst Avenue where Mr Collins, the
factory manager was interviewed and the following was
ascertained.

At about 9.30 a.m. today the Revenue Bureau official
accompanied by a S.M.C. policeman went to the factory
office and stated he wished to inspect the buildings with
a view to imposing a tax on the company. Mr Collins told
the Revenue Official that as he did not have authority
from the head office of the company, No. 233 Hamilton
House, no inspection of the buildings could be permitted.
An argument ensued during which the Revenue Official
threatened to call a squad of S.M.C. police to surround
the building and to carry out the inspection by force.
The manager then informed the Head Office who in turn
informed Well Station.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
<u>Collecting of Taxes by Officers of the Shanghai City Government Office in the Settlement.</u>

At 10.15 a.m. Thursday, May 30, 1940, a telephone message was received from the International Industrial Corporation Ltd. Inc. U.S.A. (Silk Filature), Lane 1501 House 21, Ferry Road (Yuh Loong) stating that a further letter was received by them from the Finance Bureau of the City Government of Greater Shanghai, which consists of a demand for payment of a building tax levied on the premises.

D.C. Millhouse attended and obtained a copy of this particular letter, also a copy of a letter sent by the management in answer to the first request to pay the tax.

It appears that advice was received from the American Consulate General not to pay the tax as described on the grounds that the premises are situated on a Municipal Road, furthermore no agreement has been reached between the Municipal Council and the City Government concerning the collection of taxes which the management will continue to pay to the Municipal Council. The management have brought the matter to the notice of their Head Office, No. 346 Szechuen Road for necessary action.

Copies of the two letters are attached.

SHANGHAI, May 17, 1940.

City Government of Greater Shanghai,
Bureau of Finance,
Western District Collection Office,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sirs,

With reference to your notice of May 9/40
addressed to us, we beg to inform you that our factory
is located on a Municipal Road and our taxes are paid to
the Shanghai Municipal Council.

The question of the machinery having been
removed from Chapei or any other place has no relation to
your demand for taxes.

As our Company is a duly organized American
Company and operates under American treaty rights in China,
we have referred you letter to the American Consulate
General for their information.

We are informed by our Consulate that no
agreement has been reached between the Council and the
City Government of Greater Shanghai, and until this question
of who has the right to collect taxes on our property has
been definitely determined, we should continue to pay our
taxes to the S.M.C.

Yours faithfully,

The International Industrial Corpn.

levies the house tax equally by order.

Sir,

At about 11.15 a.m. January 4, 1940, a telephone
report was received at Pootoo Road Station from C.J.Breen
& Co, Textile Department, 211 Pen (彭) Dyeworks,
(American), 211 Penang Road, G.S. (S.M.C. Tax-payer)
stating that four S.M.P. officers armed with rifles
in uniform called at the works office accompanied by an
official of the Shanghai City Government Finance Bureau
named Mr. Wong (王) at 11 a.m. above date when a
demand was made for payment of taxes. The party left the
office at about 11.05 a.m. taking with them a clerk named
Yue Sinu Poo (岳新甫), age 24, Ningpo, residing on the
premises, who was requested to go to the revenue office
on Jenfield Road.

The S.M.P. was informed and in accordance
with instructions, a visit was made to the works by
Inspector Watson and D.C.I. Tilton, where at about 12 noon
the aforementioned clerk returned. He stated that he was
escorted to the Revenue Office by the S.M.P. officers
where he was questioned concerning the refusal of the
factory management to pay taxes. The clerk stated that
the request should be made to the Head Office of the firm
at 70 Szechuen Road, where Mr. Wong Sing Liang (黃品良)
Business Manager would attend to same. The clerk was
allowed to leave the Revenue Office at 11.30 a.m. and was
told to inform Mr. Wong to call at the Revenue Office
and pay the taxes without delay.

At about 11.35 a.m. Mr. C.J. Breen (American)
Manager of the firm telephoned from the head office to

先生，

1940年1月4日上午11时15分左右，普陀路巡捕房接到来自C.J. Breen公司纺织部（美国籍），地址为戈登路槟榔路211号染厂（工部局纳税人）的电话报告，称当日上午11时，四名身着制服、手持步枪的工部局警务处（S.M.P.）警员陪同一名名为王先生（Wong）的上海市政府财政局官员前往该厂办公室，要求缴纳税款。该伙人于上午11时05分左右离开办公室，带走了一名名为岳新甫（Yue Sinu Poo）、24岁、宁波籍、居住在厂内的职员，并要求其前往静安寺路（Jenfield Road）的税务局。

工部局警务处获悉后，按照指示，由沃森督察（Inspector Watson）和副首席督察蒂尔顿（D.C.I. Tilton）前往该厂，上述职员于中午12点左右返回。他陈述称，他被工部局警务处警员护送至税务局，并因工厂管理层拒绝纳税而受到质询。该职员陈述称，应向位于四川路70号的公司总办事处提出请求，由业务经理黄品良先生（Mr. Wong Sing Liang）处理此事。该职员于上午11时30分获准离开税务局，并被告知通知黄先生立即前往税务局缴纳税款。

当日上午11时35分左右，该公司美籍经理C.J. Breen先生从总办事处致电

Yue Siau Foo.

Ningpo.
Footoo Rd 3tn        4.1.40.        translated
                                     xxxxxx    Clerk Chin Hung Kong.

My name is Yue Siau Foo, age 24, native of Ningpo,
clerk employed and residing at the C.J. Breen & Co. Textile
Department, 211 Penang Road, O.O.L.

At about 11 a.m. 4.1.40, a shroff of the Western Revenue
Department of the Shanghai City Government Finance Bureau
came to my office with four S.C.I. S.B. Policemen in uniform,
all of whom were armed with rifles. The shroff on entering
requested our factory to despatch a clerk to accompany them
to his office for the purpose of negotiating tax affairs and
produced an official letter, addressed to our factory, as
evidence. I then approached him and asked what his name was,
when he replied "Yeng." He then requested me to go with him
but I told him that I was a junior clerk in the factory,
however, he stated that it did not matter, and that I must go
and could return very soon.

Having left the factory premises, I followed them on
foot to the Western Revenue Department Office, situated at
the corner of Jessfield and Kinsear Roads. A clerk named Tsu
asked me to sit down on a chair and requested my name, age, etc
He also inquired of me as to why our factory declined to pay
them quarter taxes. I explained to them that they can
negotiate with Mr. Wong, who is attached to the Head-Office,
at 70 Szechuen Road. He then demanded that Mr. Wong should
call at his office and pay the necessary taxes without delay.
I was therefore released.

This is my true statement.

Signed Yue Siau Foo.

岳小甫（Yue Siau Foo）。

宁波。
普陀路巡捕房        1940年1月4日。        翻译
                                     xxxxxx    职员 Chin Hung Kong。

我叫岳小甫，24岁，宁波人，受雇于戈登路槟榔路211号C.J. Breen公司纺织部（O.O.L.）并居住于此，担任职员。

1940年1月4日上午11时左右，上海市政府财政局西税局的一名收款员带着四名身着制服、均携带步枪的华探特别处（S.C.I. S.B.）警员来到我的办公室。该收款员进入后，要求我厂派遣一名职员随同他前往其办公室协商税务事宜，并出示了一封致我厂的公函作为凭证。于是我上前询问他的姓名，他回答姓“杨”（Yeng）。随后他要求我随他前往，但我告诉他我只是厂里的一名初级职员，然而他表示这没关系，说我必须去，而且很快就能回来。

离开工厂后，我步行跟随他们前往位于极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）和金西尔路（Kinsear Roads）拐角处的西税局办公室。一位名为徐（Tsu）的职员让我坐在椅子上，询问了我的姓名、年龄等信息。他还询问我厂为何拒绝缴纳季度税款。我向他们解释称，他们可以与隶属于四川路70号总办事处的黄先生（Mr. Wong）协商。随后他要求黄先生立即前往其办公室缴纳必要税款。因此我被释放。

这是我的真实陈述。

签名：岳小甫。

CHINA PRESS.

DEC 8 1939

Tax Collectors
Deny Threats
To Cohen Home

For the second time in two days "Ta Tao" tax collectors called at the home of a British resident, Mrs. M. M. Cohen, at 7C Tifeng Road yesterday morning in an attempt to obtain from her municipal rates—despite a statement of the "Special Commissioner for Foreign Affairs" of the "Shanghai Special City Government" to the British Consulate-General that Britons would not be molested.

Yesterday morning Mrs. Cohen immediately notified the Bubbling Well Police Station, and members of the S.M.P. arrived at her home in time to speak with the puppet collectors. These denied that they had threatened to take drastic action, and explained merely that they were there to collect taxes—if they could get them.

The same men called at the Cohen home Wednesday night, when Mrs. Cohen was out. The collectors tried to collect taxes to the value of $27 from the servants, and finally left with the threat that, if taxes were not paid, one of the servants would be arrested and held as hostage.

Reports that a coolie of the household was kidnapped published yesterday morning, were prompted by the flight of one of the coolies, who made himself scarce when he thought for some reason that the threat was directed at him.

1939年12月8日

税务征收员
否认对
科恩住宅的威胁

继两天内第二次，“大道”（Ta Tao）税务征收员于昨天上午前往居住在提丰路7C号的英国居民M. M. 科恩夫人家中，试图向她收取市政捐税——尽管“上海特别市政府”的“外交事务专员”已向英国总领事馆声明，英国人不会受到骚扰。

昨天上午，科恩夫人立即通知了静安寺路巡捕房，工部局警务处（S.M.P.）成员及时赶到她家，与傀儡征收员交谈。这些征收员否认曾威胁采取严厉行动，并解释说他们只是来收税的——如果能收到的话。

同一批人曾在周三晚上去过科恩家，当时科恩夫人不在家。征收员试图从仆人那里收取价值27美元的税款，最后离开时威胁说，如果不缴纳税款，将逮捕一名仆人作为人质。

昨天早晨报道的关于该家庭一名苦力被绑架的消息，是由其中一名苦力的逃跑引起的，他出于某种原因认为威胁是针对他的，便躲了起来。

中国仆人被告知
绑架意图

上海特别市组织的外交事务专员已告知英国总领事馆，将向上海特别市官员下达命令，不得在外滩道路区域（outside roads area）向英国臣民征税或进行干扰。据监理领事今日正式告知《上海晚邮报》，该声明是这位专员周二访问英国总领事馆时作出的。
绑架威胁
专员的注意力被引向上周六发生的一件事，当时两名身着制服和两名便衣的上海特别市（SSM）警察造访了一位居住在愚园路某弄堂内的英国女士的家。该女士不在家，于是这四个人向中国仆人索要27美元“税款”，并称如果不支付，将扣押一名仆人作为赎金。
然而，昨天对居住在提丰路7e号的M. M. 科恩夫人提出了类似的要求，结果导致她的一名仆人因恐惧而离职。英国驻华监理领事将此次访问归因于专员的命令可能尚未传达。
不予承认
《晚邮报》获悉，英国当局被告知：“市长向居住在外滩道路区域的英国臣民征税的权利不被英国当局承认。”这一声明是周二向上海特别市专员作出的，专员承诺不再干扰英国臣民。
在过去几天里，至少有十几起外国人（包括英国人、挪威人和丹麦人）遭到“大道”当局访问并被要求缴纳税款的案例被报告。

CHINA PRESS.

DEC 7 1939

“Ta Tao” Men Seize Servant
In New Stunt To Collect Tax

One of the first open attempts of the “Shanghai Special Municipality” to collect taxes from foreigners residing on extra-Settlement roads was the object of a Shanghai Municipal Police inquiry last night.
The attempt was unsuccessful as a tax collecting venture but as a kidnapping, it proved quite an occasion. A Chinese coolie was abducted and is now being held as a hostage until a Mrs. Cohen, British subject, pays the levy demanded by the “tax collectors,” according to a report obtained by THE CHINA PRESS from authoritative quarters last night.
Mrs. Cohen reported the case to the Bubbling Well Police Station and an investigation was subsequently started. The incident occurred at 4.10 p.m. yesterday.

Several men, claiming to be “Ta Tao” authorities, called at the Cohen home on Tifeng Road and asked to see the mistress. Mrs. Cohen appeared and was told by her callers that from now on she would have to pay taxes to the “Shanghai Special Municipality.”
She reminded her visitors that she paid taxes to the Shanghai Municipal Council and had no intention of paying levies to the “Shanghai Special Municipality.”
Some argument followed whereupon the “tax collectors” finally resorted to force, seized the coolie and made him accompany them. As they left, they informed the houseboy that they would return and that unless Mrs. Cohen paid the tax, he (the houseboy) would be abducted just to teach the British woman a lesson.

1939年12月7日

“大道”人员扣押仆人
作为收税新花样

昨晚，上海公共租界工部局警务处对“上海特别市”首次公开尝试向越界筑路区域居住的外国人征税一事展开调查。
据《大美晚报》昨晚从权威渠道获得的报告称，这次行动作为收税尝试并未成功，但作为一起绑架案，却引起了不小的轰动。一名中国苦力被绑架，目前正被扣为人质，直到英籍侨民科恩夫人支付“收税人员”所要求的税款为止。
科恩夫人已向静安寺巡捕房报案，随后展开了调查。事件发生于昨日下午4时10分。

几名自称是“大道”当局的人员来到提丰路的科恩寓所，要求见女主人。科恩夫人出面后，来访者告知她，从现在起她必须向“上海特别市”缴纳税款。
她提醒来访者，她已向上海工部局纳税，无意向“上海特别市”缴纳任何捐税。
双方发生了一些争执，随后“收税人员”最终诉诸武力，劫走该名苦力并迫使其随行。离开时，他们告知男仆，他们还会回来，除非科恩夫人缴纳税款，否则他（男仆）将被绑架，以此给这位英国妇女一个教训。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
OCT 19 1939

S.M.C. WILLING TO
NEGOTIATE
Would Discuss Problems
With Shanghai City
Government

An official of the Shanghai Municipal Council was asked yesterday whether the matter of the payment of taxes by residents in the outside roads areas had passed out of the S.M.C.'s hands into those of the Consular Body. He replied that the Council still expected outside roads residents to pay rates and taxes to the S.M.C., and that, although the Consular Body was now going to deal with the question, it had not passed completely out of the S.M.C.'s hands.

There were no negotiations in progress between the Council and the Shanghai City Government at the present moment, the official said, however if the City Government approached the S.M.C. the latter would be willing to negotiate and discuss any questions brought forward.

This representative did not know when the Consular Body was going to meet, and it is believed that no date has been set by the Body to convene to discuss the question of outside roads and the payment of taxes and rates by the residents living in those areas.

It is known, however, that these questions were not on the agenda as subjects to be considered by the Council when it met yesterday evening.

1939年10月19日

工部局愿意
进行谈判
愿与上海市政府
讨论相关问题

昨日，有人询问上海工部局的一名官员，关于越界筑路区域居民缴纳税款一事，是否已从工部局手中移交至领事团处理。该官员回答说，工部局仍期望越界筑路区域的居民向工部局缴纳捐税；虽然领事团现在将处理此事，但该事并未完全脱离工部局的管辖范围。

该官员表示，目前工部局与上海市政府之间没有进行任何谈判，但如果市政府主动接触工部局，后者愿意就提出的任何问题进行谈判和讨论。

这位代表不知道领事团何时开会，据信领事团尚未确定日期召开会议以讨论越界筑路及居住在该区域居民的捐税缴纳问题。

然而，据悉这些问题并未列入昨晚工部局会议的审议议程。

Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao, T: Mei Pac, Chinese-American Daily

OUTSIDE ROAD RESIDENTS ASKED TO PAY RATES TO S.M.C.

Interviewed yesterday by our reporter, Mr. G.
Phillips, Secretary and Commissioner-General of the S.M.C.,
said that while the Council expects the residents on the
outside roads to pay rates and taxes to the Council, it
cannot take any direct action in the dispute now that the
matter is in the hands of the Consular Body.
Asked whether the Council would advise residents
of outside roads to refuse the payment of rates and taxes
to any other administration, Mr. Phillips said that he was
not in a position to answer the question.
It has also been learned from the Settlement
authorities that no date has been set by the Consular Body
for the consideration of this issue.
As the situation stands at present, with the
Shanghai City Government demanding rates and taxes from
the residents in the extra-Settlement roads area, the people
most likely to suffer are the Chinese. Foreigners enjoying
consular protection may refuse to pay rates to any
administration except the S.M.C. and will receive the support
of their respective consular representatives. There is no
authority, however, to whom Chinese may appeal for such
support, and it has by now become only too plain, according
to views expressed in foreign circles, that the S.M.C. is
not in a position to afford protection to such Chinese
residents.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
OCT 16 1939
Tax On Outside
Road Set In '06

Feetham Report Traces
SMC Efforts To Get
Municipal Rates

Following is the fourth of a series of articles reproduced from Justice Feetham's report made to the Shanghai Municipal Council in 1931, and relating to the "outside roads." On its specific points, the article deals with the origin and development of the roads, besides containing a few legal aspects of the matter, the whole shedding interesting light on the present controversy over jurisdiction in the "extra" areas. Justice Feetham's proposals on "the future of the areas," including two schemes to provide a solution, will be published subsequently.)

At that time negotiations were in progress with the Shanghai Waterworks Company for a new agreement to be entered into between the Company and the Council as to water supply. The Council, following the example which had previously been set by the Council of the French Concession in regard to the supply of water to the occupants of houses abutting on its road outside the Concession, proposed to the Water Company that the clause in the new agreement which provided that the Company was to supply water not only to residents in the Settlement but also to residents on Council roads outside the Settlement, should include the following proviso:—

No Water "Outside"
Provided that the Company shall not deliver water to any resident without the Settlement, in the absence of an agreement existing at the date of these presents as to such supply, except during such time as such resident shall remain bound by agreement with the Council to pay, in respect of any premises a special tax not exceeding such monthly rates and taxes as may from time to time be payable in respect of similar premises situated within the Settlement.

When the proposed agreement with the Waterworks Company was submitted to the ratepayers at their annual meeting on March 21, 1905, this clause was discussed. The Chairman of the Council, in recommending the ratepayers to approve of the proposed arrangement stated that he felt sure that the justice and expediency of the proposed measure would be readily admitted, as a measure universally applicable which imposed a reasonable amount of taxation on those who enjoyed "practically all the benefits of municipal administration."

There was some criticism of the proposal by one of the residents, in the area affected, and it appears from his statement that at that time the Settlement Fire Brigade did not undertake the protection of houses on the outside roads. The agreement, including the proposed proviso, was approved by the meeting.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》
1939年10月16日

越界筑路税收
始于1906年

费唐报告追溯
工部局征收市政捐税的努力

以下是从1931年费唐法官（Justice Feetham）向上海工部局提交的报告中摘录的一系列文章中的第四篇，内容涉及“越界筑路”。就该报告的具体要点而言，本文探讨了这些道路的起源和发展，此外还包含该事项的一些法律层面，整体为当前关于“越界”区域管辖权的争议提供了有趣的视角。费唐法官关于“该区域未来”的建议，包括两项提供解决方案的方案，将在后续刊登。）

当时，工部局正与上海自来水公司就签订新的供水协议进行谈判。工部局效仿法租界公董局此前针对向其界外道路沿线房屋住户供水的先例，向自来水公司提议，在新协议中规定公司不仅应向租界内居民供水，还应向工部局在租界外道路上的居民供水，该条款应包含以下 proviso（附带条件）：—

界外无水供应
前提是，除非在本协议签署之日已存在关于此类供水的协议，否则公司不得向任何租界外居民供水，除非该居民仍受与工部局签订的协议约束，承诺就任何房产缴纳特别税，该税额不超过租界内类似房产不时需缴纳的月度捐税。

1905年3月21日，在与自来水公司的拟议协议提交给纳税人年会审议时，对该条款进行了讨论。工部局主席在建议纳税人批准拟议安排时表示，他确信这项普遍适用的措施所体现的公正性和权宜性将 readily admitted（轻易被承认），因为它对那些享受“几乎所有市政管理利益”的人征收了合理数量的税款。

受影响区域的一名居民对该提议提出了一些批评，从其陈述来看，当时租界救火会并不承担越界筑路房屋的消防保护工作。包括拟议附带条件在内的协议获得了会议批准。

Rate Fixed
In pursuance of this arrange-
ment, the budget resolution passed
at the Annual Meeting the follow-
ing year, 1906, provided for a rate
at five per cent on assessed
rentals of houses beyond Settle-
ment limits, the rate on houses
inside the Settlement being 10 per
cent. The Council's report for 1906
includes the following statement
from the overseer of taxes with
regard to the collection of this
rates:—
The collection of the rate on
the rentals of houses beyond Set-
tlement limits, under provision of
the agreement with the Shanghai
Waterworks Company, Ltd., from
April 1, 1906, at first met with
some opposition from native
owners and their tenants, which
was, however, gradually overcome
and the rate paid.
It appears from the particulars
given that the amount collected
for the last three quarters of that
year amounted to Taels 2123 in
respect of 119 foreign houses, and
Taels 3282 in respect of 2024 na-
tive houses.
Chapel Body Develops
The report deals in some detail
with the difficulties that arose
with regard to the collection of
the rate from Chinese. It was at
this time that steps were being
taken to establish a Chinese
Works Bureau for North Sinza,
which eventually developed into
the Chapel Municipality. It is
stated in the report that the op-
position to the levy on the part
of the Chinese sprang "not from
any doubt as to its fairness, or
any willingness, on the part of
those concerned to pay their share
of the cost of the public main-
tenance of the neighborhood,
but as part of an organized
movement in the direction of a
distinct native administrative
bureau".
A satisfactory settlement of the
question for the time being seems
to have been reached on the un-
derstanding that the water rate
was to be collected not from the
tenants, but from the landlords of
the houses to which water was
supplied. In July, 1906, the Taotai
issued a proclamation on the sub-
ject, in which it is stated that
"The Taotai, having considered
the whole matter repeatedly, has
come to the conclusion that if the
landlords make use of the water
pipes, it is for the con-
venience of the tenants, and
the idea is, of course, excel-
lent, since renters who make use
of the water gain advantages of
a sanitary nature and immunity
from fire. It seems, therefore,
within reason that there should be
a water rate. According, however,
to the regulations within the Set-
tlement charges for water are in-
cluded in rent, and under these
circumstances this rate in the
above localities should also be paid
by the landlords so that the proce-
dure may be uniform.... I look
to residents of all classes in the
district in question, one and all
to take note that hereafter, with
the exception of those houses
which do not use the water, and
who therefore need make no pay-
ment, the rate will be paid by the
landlords."
Utilities Sign Agreements
A provision similar to that con-
tained in the Waterworks agree-
ment was subsequently inserted in
the agreements between the Coun-
cil and the Telephone Company
and between the Council's Electri-
city Department and the con-
sumers of electricity outside the
Settlement limits; and later, when
the Electricity Department was
sold provision was made that a
similar clause should be inserted
by the Shanghai Power Company
in their agreement with outside
consumers.

税率确定
根据这一安排，次年（1906年）年度会议通过的预算决议规定，对租界界限以外房屋的评估租金征收百分之五的捐税，而租界以内房屋的捐税率为百分之十。工部局1906年度报告收录了税务监督员关于此项捐税征收情况的如下陈述：——

根据与上海自来水有限公司协议的条款，自1906年4月1日起，对租界界限以外房屋租金征收捐税一事，起初遭到中国业主及其租户的一些反对，但这种反对逐渐被克服，捐税得以缴纳。

从所提供的细节来看，该年最后三个季度征收的金额总计为：119幢外籍人房屋银2123两，2024幢华人房屋银3282两。

教堂区机构的发展
报告详细论述了在向华人征收捐税方面出现的困难。当时正采取措施为北新泾（North Sinza）建立一个华人工程局，该机构后来发展成为蒲淞市公所（Chapel Municipality）。报告指出，华人方面对征税的反对，“并非出于对其公平性的任何怀疑，也非有关各方不愿承担社区公共维护费用的份额，而是作为朝着建立独立的华人行政机构方向发展的有组织运动的一部分”。

目前看来，这一问题已达成令人满意的暂时解决，其理解基础是：水费不应向租户征收，而应向供水房屋的房东征收。1906年7月，道台就此发布告示，其中称：“道台经反复考量全案，得出结论认为，若房东使用水管，乃是为了租户之便利，此意当然极佳，因为使用水的租客可获得卫生方面的益处及免于火灾之虞。因此，征收水费似在情理之中。然而，根据租界内的规章，水费包含在租金之内，在此情况下，上述地区的水费亦应由房东支付，以便程序统一____ 本人望该地区各类居民均予注意，此后，除不使用自来水因而无需付款的房屋外，水费将由房东支付。”

公用事业签署协议
随后，在与电话公司的协议中，以及工部局电力处与租界界限以外的电力消费者之间，均插入了与自来水公司协议中包含的类似条款；后来，当电力处出售时，规定上海电力公司应在其与外部消费者的协议中插入类似条款。

By this system of arrangements
based on contracts between the
Council and public utility Com-
panies, the Council has, therefore,
been able to collect a regular re-
venue from the occupants of pre-
mises on the external roads who
obtain the benefit of the services
of any such Companies.

From 1906 to 1920 the Special
Rate, which was the name given
to the rate levied on rentals of
houses on external roads, was
levied at a percentage rate
which was only half of
that at which the General Rate
was levied inside the Settlement.
It was increased in 1907 from five
to six per cent, and stood at the
latter figure till 1919, when it was
raised to seven per cent. From
1921 onwards the Special Rate has
been levied at a percentage rate
only two per cent below that at
which the General Rate inside the
Settlement has been levied, the
highest figure reached being 14
per cent.

As has already been indicated,
the conditions of the districts in
which the Council's external roads
extended were, at the dates when
the land was acquired and the
roads were made, for the most
part of a purely rural character.
During the first 40 years of the
development of the described—
that is, up to about the year 1906,
—there was no attempt on the
part of Chinese authorities to pro-
vide any form of administration
for these districts beyond such as
was normally available, under a
system of local government of a
semi-patriarchal type, to meet the
needs of Chinese country villages
and their rural inhabitants. So
far as concerned the municipal ad-
ministration of the type adapted
to the requirements of a modern
urban and suburban community
foreign and Chinese, there was an
administrative vacuum, and it was
owing to the existence of this va-
cuum that the gradual, extension of
the Council's activities became not
only possible but practically in-
evitable.
page_data.zh:
因此，通过这种基于工部局与公用事业公司之间合同的安排体系，工部局得以从那些享受此类公司服务利益的外部道路房屋占用者那里收取常规收入。

从1906年至1920年，特别捐（Special Rate，即对位于外部道路房屋租金征收的捐税名称）按百分比税率征收，该税率仅为租界内一般捐（General Rate）税率的一半。1907年，该税率从百分之五增至百分之六，并维持在该水平直至1919年，随后提高至百分之七。自1921年起，特别捐按比租界内一般捐税率低两个百分点的百分比税率征收，最高达到百分之十四。

如前所述，在工部局外部道路延伸的地区，在征地和筑路之时，其状况大多纯属乡村性质。在上述描述的发展过程的前40年中——即直到大约1906年——中国当局并未试图为这些地区提供任何形式的行政管理，除了那种在半家长式地方治理体系下通常可用的、旨在满足中国乡村及其农村居民需求的行政方式。至于适应现代城市和郊区社区（包括外籍人和华人）需求的市政管理类型，则存在行政真空；正是由于这种真空的存在，工部局活动的逐步扩展不仅成为可能，而且实际上变得不可避免。

这伙警员要求该妇女缴纳税款，当她请求本月晚些时候再来时，他们要求她立即支付。随后，该妇女被用汽车带往罗宾森路（Robison Road）市公安局分区捕房（S.C.S. S.B. Sub-station），在那里被拘留，随后被转移至极司菲尔路92号，一直拘留至1939年9月8日下午4时30分，当时其丈夫前来探望并立即支付了4幢房屋的税款共计48美元，其中2幢归他所有，另2幢归同一建筑群内的一位朋友所有。其丈夫还被要求并支付了一笔3.00美元的罚款。

(2) 俞郭氏（Yiu Koh Sz），60岁，安徽人，已婚，住胶州路旁老闸里7号，越界筑路区（O.O.L.），来到捕房报案。

据悉，1939年9月2日下午，两名市政府官方收税员来到她们家中收税。当上述两名女子告知她们已缴纳工部局（S.M.C.）捐税时，收税员称她们仍须缴纳税款。他们还声称，若当天下午不缴纳上述税款，将被逮捕。捕房告知这两名投诉人回家，如果再次受到市政府官员的骚扰或传唤，应立即通知捕房。

1939年9月7日《事故记录簿》摘录。

当日上午10时30分，华捕3226号从第12号街头电话亭致电捕房，报告称市政府收税员正试图向胶州路旁老闸里（越界筑路区）的居民收税。已告知负责警官，指示是相关住户应向工部局财务处报告此案。下午4时，工部局福里斯特先生（Mr. Forrister）

Revenue Department came to the station and stated that
he had visited the above mentioned alleyway, which, he
states, is a "Cul-de-sac" and therefore is untaxable

reached by the S.M.C. and City Government. Mr. Forrister
also stated that one of the residents had been arrested
and taken to the S.C.G.P.B. Station at 92 Jessfield Road.

Enquiries made by D.S.I. Tilton, U.S. Mori and
D.I. Voong Pah Zung, disclosed that at about 10.30 a.m.
7.9.39. six unarmed uniformed and two plain clothes
officers of the S.C.G.P.B. visited No. 7 Ts Lai Li,
Kiaochow Road, O.O.L. where they interviewed Yue Koh Sz
(俞郭氏), age 60, wife of the supervisor of this block
of buildings consisting of 20 houses and shops named
Yue Tsung Ziang (俞振祥), who was absent at the time.

The party of officers requested the woman to pay
the taxes due and on her request to come again later in
the month, they demanded she pay them immediately. The
woman was then taken away by motor car to the S.C.G.P.B.
Sub-station, Robison Road, where she was detained and
later removed to No. 92 Jessfield Road and detained
until 4.30 p.m. 8.9.39. when her husband visited her
and immediately paid a total of $48. as taxes on 4
houses, 2 of which are owned by him and 2 owned by a
friend in the same block of premises. A further sum
of $3.00 was demanded and paid by the husband as a fine.

The above man Yue Tsung Ziang and his wife were
called to Pootoo Road Station at 10 a.m. 9.9.39. and

日期：1939年9月9日。19时
事由续。（第2页）。
制表人 转呈人

税务局人员来到巡捕房并称，
他已视察上述弄堂，据他称，该弄堂为“死胡同”，因此根据工部局与市政府达成的某些口头协议，免予市政府征税。福里斯特（Forrister）先生还称，一名居民已被逮捕并带往极司菲尔路92号的上海市警察局巡捕房。

经副督察长蒂尔顿（Tilton）、美国籍警员森（Mori）及督察冯柏松（Voong Pah Zung，音译）调查，查明在1939年9月7日上午10时30分左右，六名身着制服的未携带武器警员和两名便衣警员（隶属上海市警察局）前往胶州路俞家里7号（外侨居留地），询问了该处住户俞郭氏（Yue Koh Sz），现年60岁，系由20栋房屋和店铺组成的这一街区的管理人俞振祥（Yue Tsung Ziang）之妻，当时俞振祥不在场。

这伙警员要求该妇女缴纳税款，在她请求本月晚些时候再来时，他们要求她立即支付。随后，该妇女被汽车带往罗宾森路（Robison Road，即今延安东路）的上海市警察局分巡捕房，在那里被拘留，随后又被转移至极司菲尔路92号，一直拘留至1939年9月8日下午4时30分，其丈夫前来看望并立即支付了4栋房屋的税款共计48元，其中2栋归其所有，另2栋归同一街区的一位朋友所有。其丈夫还被要求并支付了一笔3.00元的罚款。

上述男子俞振祥及其妻子于1939年9月9日上午10时被召至普陀路巡捕房，并出示了如上所述的4张税单收据。

page_data.en:
Revenue Officers
Detained

Britons, Chinese are
Detained for Five Hours
When Collecting Taxes

Chief Revenue Inspector F. J.
Forrest, Assistant Inspector A. J.
Griffith, and a Chinese clerk, all em-
ployees of the Revenue Office, Shang-
hai Municipal Council, were detained
at a "Ta Tao" police station off
Edinburgh Road for five hours on
Tuesday afternoon after they had
called at House 15, Lane 95 Edinburgh
Road, shortly after 2 p.m., to make
enquiries regarding the retention by
the occupants of the place, of a
receipt, which was taken from a
Revenue Office employee earlier the
same day, without the money having
been paid.

Following lengthy conversations
between S. M. P. officials and Mr.
Kitaoka, Japanese adviser to the "Ta
Tao" government, three men were
released at 7.15 p.m. the same day.

The whole incident started in the
morning hours, when the tenant of
House 15 was asked to pay the quar-
terly rates due. He asked to be
shown the receipt under the pretext
that he must first take it to his em-
ployer. The receipt was handed
over, and subsequently given to a
"Ta Tao" official in plain-clothes who
had evidently given instructions to
the tenants of the house in question
to inform him when demands for the
payment of rates would be made.

Upon being informed of the oc-
currence, Mr. Forrest accompanied
by Mr. Griffith and the same shroff,
called on the occupant of the house
in the afternoon, with the request for
payment of the rates. The man at
the door asked them to enter and to
wait for a few minutes.

"Ta Tao" Official Arrives

Shortly afterwards, the plain-
clothes "Ta Tao" official arrived at
the house accompanied by a number
of armed policemen of the Japanese-
occupied territory and asked the
party to accompany him to the police
station, which they did.

A discussion regarding the rights
of the Shanghai Municipal Council
to collect rates in "Ta Tao" territory
ensued and about one hour later,
when the Council employees wished
to leave, they were informed that
they were not free to do so. Mr.
Forrest was permitted, however, to
order the car which had conveyed
his party to the address and which
was parked on Edinburgh Road, to
return to the office and first informa-
tion of the affair was received by
Revenue Office officials shortly after
4 p.m. A police party from Bubbling
Well Police Station was immediately
formed and first called on the
Japanese Gendarmerie headquarters
on Westfield Road from where they
were referred to the "Ta Tao" police
station where the two Britons and
the Chinese were being detained.

Passage Blocked
page_data.zh:
税务官员
被拘

英籍和华人官员
收税时被扣留五小时

首席税务督察 F. J.
福里斯特（Forrest）、助理督察 A. J.
格里菲斯（Griffith）以及一名华籍职员，均为上
海公共租界工部局税务处的雇员，于周二下午
在爱丁堡路附近的“大道”警察局被扣留了五
个小时。此前，他们在下午2点后不久曾前往
爱丁堡路95弄15号，就当天早些时候从一名
税务处雇员手中拿走的一张收据一事进行查
询，该收据是在未付款的情况下被拿走的。

经过工部局警务处官员与“大道”政府日本
顾问北冈（Kitaoka）先生的长时间交谈后，三
人于当晚7时15分获释。

整个事件始于上午时段，当时15号的租户
被要求支付到期的季度捐税。他以必须先将
收据交给雇主为借口，要求查看收据。收据
被交出，随后交给了一名便衣“大道”官员，
该官员显然已指示该房屋的租户，在有征收
捐税的要求时通知他。

得知此事后，福里斯特先生在格里菲斯先
生和同一名出纳员的陪同下，于下午前往该
房屋，要求支付捐税。门口的人请他们进屋
并等待几分钟。

“大道”官员抵达

不久之后，那名便衣“大道”官员在多名
日占区武装警察的陪同下来到该房屋，并要
求一行人随他前往警察局，他们照办了。

随后就上海公共租界工部局在“大道”辖
区内征收捐税的权利问题展开了讨论，大约
一小时后，当工部局雇员希望离开时，他们
被告知不得离开。不过，福里斯特先生被允
许命令那辆将他们送到该地址并停在爱丁堡
路上的汽车返回办公室，税务处官员在下午
4点后不久收到了关于此事的第一手消息。
静安寺巡捕房立即组建了一支警察小队，首
先前往西菲尔德路（Westfield Road，即今西康
路）的日本宪兵队总部，随后被指引至“大
道”警察局，两名英籍人士和一名华人正被
关押在那里。

通道受阻

page_data.en:
On entering the alleyway, the
police party was confronted by a
large number of armed "Ta Tao"
policemen who refused to let them
pass at first but finally agreed to
permit them to proceed to the police
station where Mr. Kitaoka already
awaited them and where meanwhile
large reinforcements of "Ta Tao"
policemen had arrived.
After lengthy conversations, Mr.
Kitaoka finally permitted the detain-
ed men to leave on the understanding
that the general question of the
collection of rates by the Shanghai
Municipal Council in extra-settle-
ment Roads would be taken up with
the Council.

Collections Continue

Questioned yesterday, an official of
the Revenue Office stated that em-
ployees of the office were continuing
to collect rates in the Western area
and had not been interfered with
since.
The lane in which the house in
question and the "Ta Tao" police
station are situated, is the one where
a shoot-up between an S. M. P.
search-party and a gang of armed
men occurred on the afternoon of
July 2 and it is here too, where the
lair of some 150 armed gangsters is
situated.
page_data.zh:
进入弄堂后，
警察小队面对大量武装的“大道”警察，
起初拒绝让他们通过，但最终同意允许他
们前往警察局，北冈先生已在那里等候，
同时大量“大道”警察增援部队也已抵达。
经过长时间的交谈，北冈先生最终允许
被扣人员离开，前提是上海公共租界工部
局将在越界筑路区域征收捐税的一般性问
题上与工部局进行交涉。

征税仍在继续

昨日接受询问时，税务处的一名官员表示，
该处雇员继续在西区征收捐税，此后未受
干扰。
涉案房屋和“大道”警察局所在的弄堂，
正是7月2日下午工部局警务处搜查队与一
伙武装分子发生枪战的地方，这里也是约
150名武装匪徒的巢穴所在地。

page_data.en:
Bubbling Well
25th., July 39. /
Re Detention of S.M.C. Revenue Officers by the S.M.C.
Police Bureau Authorities.
xx nd Inspector MacFarlane, .i/c.

Sir:
I beg to report that at 4.5. .m. 25-7-3 .. telephone
message was received from the S.M.C. Revenue Department,
to the effect that two Foreign members and one Chinese
member of their staff were being detained by the S. M. C.
Police at the Bureau on Edinburgh Road.
The D.C. "B" was informed and instructions were
received to make enquiries as to the reason and if
possible to obtain their release.
Acting under these instructions the undersigned
accompanied by Inspectors Tabrum and Yamaguchi proceeded
to the Headquarters of the Western Branch of the Shanghai
City Government, 32 Jessfield Road.
At this place the party met Mr. Kitaoka, Adviser to
this Bureau, and information was requested as to why the
mentioned S.M.C. Revenue officers were being detained.
Mr. Kitaoka stated that he had just been informed
of the affair and had already informed his superiors at
the Shanghai City Government at Kiangwan by phone and was
awaiting instructions.
At this point Mr. Kitaoka was asked if the Police
party could interview the detained men at the Edinburgh
Road Sub Station and Mr. Kitaoka replied in the affirmative.
The mentioned officers then proceeded to the Sub
Station and there met Mr. F.J. Forrest, Mr. A.J. Griffith
Inspectors of the S.M.C. Revenue Department, and a
Chinese Tax Collector named Yang Tsong Chang.
page_data.zh:
静安寺
1939年7月25日 /
关于工部局警务当局扣留工部局税务官员事。
xx 督察麦克法兰（MacFarlane），主管。

先生：
谨此报告，1939年7月25日下午4时..分，
接到工部局税务处的电话消息，称其两名
外籍职员和一名华籍职员正被工部局警察
拘禁在爱丁堡路的局内。
已通知B区副督察长，并收到指示，查询
原因并尽可能争取释放他们。
根据这些指示，签署人会同塔布鲁姆
（Tabrum）督察和山口（Yamaguchi）督察前
往上海市政府西区分局总部，地址为极司
菲尔路32号。
在该处，一行人会见了该局顾问北冈先
生，并要求提供有关为何扣留上述工部局
税务官员的信息。
北冈先生称，他刚刚获悉此事，并已通
过电话向位于江湾的上海市政府上级汇报，
正在等待指示。
此时，北冈先生被问及警察小队是否可
以在爱丁堡路分巡捕房会见被扣人员，北
冈先生给予了肯定答复。
随后，上述警官前往分巡捕房，在那里
会见了工部局税务处督察 F.J. 福里斯特先
生、A.J. 格里菲斯先生，以及一名名为杨宗
昌（Yang Tsong Chang，音译）的华籍收税员。

page_data.en:
-Sheet 2-

From Mr. Forrest it was learned that at bout 10.45
a.m. 28-7-39 the Revenue Department Shroff, Mr. Yang
proceeded to House No.15, Lane 505, Edinburgh Road (S.M.C.
House No., in order to collect the taxes due to the
S.M.C. At this place the Shroff met a Chinese female who
on being informed by him that he had called to collect
the taxes, asked that he wait until she called her master
After a few minutes a male Chinese in plain clothes
came on the scene accompanied by a S.C.G. Police officer
who then seized the tax receipt papers in possession of
the Shroff.
After a short argument the Police Officer returned
all the receipts with the exception of the one for House
No.15, Lane 505 Edinburgh Road and allowed the Shroff to
leave the alleyway.
The Shroff then proceeded to the Revenue Department
and made his report to Mr. Forrest, who made arrangements
with Mr. Griffith (the Inspector actually in charge of
this area) and the Shroff to return in the afternoon to
Edinburgh Road in order to check on the Shroff's state-
ment and also to obtain the return of the missing
receipt.
The two Foreigners and the Chinese arrived at House
15, Lane 505, Edinburgh Road, at about 3.15 p.m. 28-7-39
and commenced enquiries. During these enquiries the
owner of this block of property approached Mr. Forrest
and complained regarding some flood water being allowed
to remain at the rear of the houses. Mr. Forrest viewed
page_data.zh:
-第2页-

从福里斯特先生处获悉，1939年7月28日
上午10时45分左右，税务处出纳员杨先生前
往爱丁堡路505弄15号（工部局门牌号），
以收取欠工部局的税款。在该处，出纳员
遇到一名中国妇女，当他告知她是来收税
时，该妇女让他等待，直到她叫来主人。
几分钟后，一名身穿便衣的中国男子在一
名上海市警察局警员的陪同下来到现场，
该警员随即没收了出纳员持有的税单收据。
经过简短争论后，该警员归还了除爱丁
堡路505弄15号以外的所有收据，并允许出
纳员离开弄堂。
出纳员随后前往税务处，向福里斯特先
生作了报告，福里斯特先生与该地区实际
负责人格里菲斯督察及出纳员安排于下午
返回爱丁堡路，以核实出纳员的陈述，并
追回丢失的收据。
两名外籍人士和这名华人于1939年7月28
日下午3时15分左右到达爱丁堡路505弄15
号，并开始查询。在此期间，该街区的业
主走近福里斯特先生，投诉允许积水留在
房屋后方的问题。福里斯特先生查看了

page_data.en:
-heet 3-

the re complained of and returned after lapse of
bout 10 minutes to find six S.C.C. Police officers, one
armed with rifle, standing outside house No. 15, together
with a male Chinese only attired in underclothing. The
latter asked Mr. Forrest for pass and when told that he
had no pass and did not require one, was informed that he
would have to go to the local bureau. The Revenue Dept.
Officers agreed and the whole party then proceeded to the
Edinburgh Road S.C.C. Police Sub Station via a connecting
alleyway from Lane 808 Edinburgh Road.

At the Police Sub Station Mr. Forrest began making
enquiries as to the reason for the seizure of the Tax
Receipt from the Shroff and the only reply he could get
was that they had had instructions to do so and that Mr.
Kitaoka was being informed. According to Mr. Forrest,
the Officer-in-charge of the Bureau telephoned to 92
Jessfield Road on eight occasions and each time was
informed that Mr Kitaoka was on his way there.

These endeavours to get in touch with Mr. Kitaoka
occupied almost 45 minutes and at about 4 p.m. about 20
S.C.C. Police Officers arrived at the Sub Station, making
a total of about 40 officers in all.

When Mr. Forrest began to realize that they were
not getting on with the enquiries he instructed that Mr.
Griffiths return to the Revenue Department in order to
attend to routine matters in the office. It was then
discovered that they were actually detained when per-
mission was refused to allow Mr. Griffiths to leave.
page_data.zh:
-第3页-

被投诉的区域，并在大约10分钟后返回，
发现六名上海市警察局警员（其中一人持
步枪）站在15号房屋外，旁边还有一名只
穿内衣的中国男子。后者向福里斯特先生
索要通行证，当被告知他没有通行证且无
需通行证时，对方告知他必须去当地局里。
税务处官员表示同意，随后全体人员经由
爱丁堡路808弄的一条连接弄堂前往爱丁堡
路上海市警察局分巡捕房。

在分巡捕房，福里斯特先生开始询问没
收出纳员税单收据的原因，但他得到的唯
一答复是他们奉命行事，且已通知北冈先
生。据福里斯特先生称，该局负责人八次
致电极司菲尔路92号，每次均被告知北冈
先生正在前往那里。

这些试图联系北冈先生的努力耗费了将
近45分钟，下午4点左右，约20名上海市警
察局警员到达分巡捕房，使总人数达到约
40人。

当福里斯特先生开始意识到调查无法取
得进展时，他指示格里菲斯先生返回税务
处以处理办公室的日常事务。此时才发现，
由于拒绝允许格里菲斯先生离开，他们实
际上已被拘留。

page_data.en:
-Sheet 4-

Mr. Forrest then asked that the Shroff be allowed
to go out to the roadway in order to tell his chauffeur
not to wait. The Shroff was escorted to Edinburgh Road
and he was able to convey to the chauffeur that the
party was being detained and to return to the Revenue
Office and to report.

The Revenue Department then informed the Bubbling
Well Police Station as stated.

Having ascertained how matters stood the Police party
then returned to 92 Jessfield Road and again interviewed
Mr. Kitaoka and informed him of the situation as far as
could be ascertained by the S.M.C. Police.

Mr. Kitaoka replied that he had tried to get into
touch with Mr. Fu Shiao-an, Mayor of the Greater Shanghai
in order to obtain instructions regarding the matter but
had failed.

The Police party then attempted to impress on Mr.
Kitaoka that the Revenue Officers had merely been carry-
ing out their task and had gone to Edinburgh Road in
order to get an explanation for the act of the S.M.C.
Police Officer and also that they had voluntarily gone
to the Sub Station to further their enquiries.

Mr. Kitaoka replied that he understood the situat-
ion and would order the release of detained men on
condition that the S.M.C. would refrain in future from
collecting taxes from premises in territory under the
Shanghai City Government.

He was informed that as Police Officers the party

被护送至爱丁堡路，他得以向司机传达一

税务处随后按所述通知了静安寺巡捕房。

在查明情况后，警察小队随后返回极司
菲尔路92号，再次会见北冈先生，并向他
通报了工部局警务处所能查明的情况。

北冈先生回复称，他曾试图联系大上海
市长傅筱庵（Fu Shiao-an，音译）以获取关
于此事的指示，但未成功。

警察小队随后试图向北冈先生强调，税
务官员 merely 是在执行任务，前往爱丁堡
路是为了就上海市警察局警员的行为寻求
解释，并且他们是自愿前往分巡捕房以推
进调查的。

北冈先生回复称，他理解这一情况，并
将下令释放被扣人员，条件是工部局今后
不再向上海市政府管辖区域内的房产征收
税款。

他被告知，作为警务人员，一行人

could only convey my verbal statement he might wish to
make. He then added that he would order the release of
the men detained if it were conveyed to the S.M.C. that
it was to be understood in future, that any S.M.C. Tax
Collector, entering territory controlled by them would be
detained.

Also, that the S.M.C. were only entitled to collect
taxes from premises actually abutting onto Municipal roads and
that only only the City Government was entitled to collect
taxes from houses in alleyways whether cul-de-sac or
otherwise.

With this the Police party withdrew from 92 Jessfield
Road and proceeded to Edinburgh Road Sub Station accompani-
ed by Chief Inspector Wong Tuh Ling of the S.C.U. Police
Bureau.

On arrival at Edinburgh Road Sub Station Chief
Inspector Wong Tuh Ling ordered the release of Mr. Forrest
Mr. Griffiths and Shroff Yang. The tax paper was returned
to Mr. Forrest at about 6.40 p.m.

The entire party then proceeded to Bubbling Well
Police Station where Mr. Forrest made his report to his
superiors.

At the time that the S.M. Police party left the Sub
Station, the 20 odd S.C.U. Police who had been "standing
by" were also seen to leave in cars.

此外，工部局仅有权对实际上毗邻市政道路的房产征收税款，而只有市政府才有权对弄堂内的房屋（无论是死胡同还是其他类型）征收税款。

至此，警务人员从极司菲尔路92号撤离，并在特别市警察局（S.C.U. Police Bureau）的黄杜林（Wong Tuh Ling，音译）总督察的陪同下，前往爱丁堡路分巡捕房。

抵达爱丁堡路分巡捕房后，黄杜林总督察下令释放福雷斯特先生（Mr. Forrest）、格里菲斯先生（Mr. Griffiths）和杨账房（Shroff Yang）。税单于下午6时40分左右归还给福雷斯特先生。

当工部局警务人员离开分巡捕房时，那二十余名一直“待命”的特别市警察也被看到乘车离开。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JUL 27 193⁰

SMC Revenue
Officials Held

Ta Tao Police Arrest
British Collectors
In Badlands

While Mr. H. Rose and his
PWD party were still in custody
of the Ta Tao municipality at the
Civic Center, two British mem-
bers of the SMC Revenue Staff
were held, for five hours by Ta
Tao police in the badlands, on
Tuesday afternoon and evening.
These two were Mr. F. J.
Forrest, Chief Inspector, and Mr.
A. J. Griffith, Assistant Inspector.
They had been collecting taxes in
a badlands alleyway, Lane -95
Edinburgh Road, close to the
hang-out of terrorist gunmen.
Polite Request
The pair went down the alley-
way shortly after 2 p.m. Tuesday.
At 2.15, a group of Ta Tao police
came up to them, and asked them
politely to accompany them to
their sub-station, which was at
the end of the lane. There was
nothing else to do but comply.
After an hour, the office car
which the pair had used was
sent off so that the chauffeur
might report the detention.
Officers from Bubbling Well
Station got on the job, and were
met by Mr. Kitaoka, Western
District Adviser to the Ta Tao
municipality. They secured the
release of the Britons at 7.15
p.m.
Old Problem
Reason for the detention was
that the Ta Tao authorities were
challenging the right of the
Shanghai Municipal Council to
collect rates down the alleyway,
off a municipal road, the same
trouble as occurred with the
former city government.
SMC officials today told the
Shanghai Evening Post that the
Council considered itself entitled
to remuneration for services
rendered, as alleyway dwellers
enjoyed the use of public utilities
of access to municipal roads and
use of the drainage system.

（批：Q 28/7）

193⁰年7月27日

工部局税收
官员被扣

大盗警察在
歹土逮捕
英国收税员

当H. Rose先生及其公共工程处（PWD）一行人仍被大盗市政府拘押在市中心时，两名工部局税务处的英国成员于周二下午及晚间，在歹土地区被大盗警察扣留了五个小时。这两人是总督察F. J. Forrest先生和助理督察A. J. Griffith先生。他们当时正在爱丁堡路95弄的一条歹土弄堂里征收税款，该地靠近恐怖枪手的巢穴。

礼貌的请求

这对搭档于周二下午2点后不久进入该弄堂。2点15分，一群大盗警察走近他们，礼貌地要求他们陪同前往位于弄堂尽头的分驻所。除了照办之外别无他法。一小时后，两人使用的办公用车被遣返，以便司机报告拘留情况。静安寺捕房的警官介入此事，并会见了大盗市政府西区顾问北冈先生（Mr. Kitaoka）。他们在晚上7点15分确保了这两名英国人的获释。

老问题

拘留的原因是，大盗当局质疑工部局在偏离市政道路的弄堂内征收捐税的权利，这与前市政府发生过的纠纷相同。工部局官员今日告诉《上海晚邮报》，理事会认为其有权就所提供的服务获得报酬，因为弄堂居民享有使用公共设施、通往市政道路以及使用排水系统的权利。

（批注：Q 28/7）

A MALE CHINESE ARRESTED BY THE TA TAO POLICE.
---------------------------------------------

At 10 a.m. 19-9-38 a telephone message was received
from the Ta Zung(大盛) Wine Shop, 46 Edinburgh Road, to
the effect that their accountant Jung Foong Kung(陳芳根)
had been arrested by the Ta Tao Police.

Immediately following the call the proprietor of the
said shop named Yong Boo King(黃伯慶) came to the
Station and made the following report:

The above shop had been regularly paying taxes to
the S.M.C., but lately several attempts have been made to
collect taxes by the Ta Tao officials.

The management wrote a letter to the S.M.C. and
received an answer advising them that it was within their
rights to oppose the new taxation and that they could
rely upon the assistance of S.M.C.(The letter from S.M.C.
Secretariat bearing reference No.A1/3).

At 9.45 a.m. 19-9-38 the Ta Tao tax collectors
accompanied by uniform constables came again to the said
shop and when the payment of rates was refused they
arrested the above named accountant and took him to the
Edinburgh Road Sub Station of the Ta Tao Police.

The undersigned accompanied by S.I. Yamagishi proceed-

一名华籍男子被大盗警察逮捕。
---

1938年9月19日上午10时，收到爱丁堡路46号大盛（Ta Zung）酒肆的电话留言，称其会计陈芳根（Jung Foong Kung，音译）被大盗警察逮捕。

紧随电话之后，该店店主黄伯庆（Yong Boo King，音译）来到捕房，作了如下报告：

上述店铺一直定期向工部局缴纳税款，但最近大盗官员多次试图征税。

管理层致函工部局，并收到回复，建议他们有权反对新税收，并可依靠工部局的协助。（工部局秘书处的信函，参考编号A1/3）。

1938年9月19日上午9时45分，大盗收税员在身穿制服的警员陪同下再次来到该店，当拒绝缴纳捐税时，他们逮捕了上述会计，并将其带至大盗警察的爱丁堡路分驻所。

署名人在山岸警佐（S.I. Yamagishi，音译）的陪同下，前往日军特科西办事处主任北片先生（Mr. Kitaska，音译）的办公室，并

case and release the arrested man. As to the taxation
in respect of the premises for which S.M.C. rates had
been already paid, Mr. Kitaoka stated he intended to
bring this question to the notice of his superior with a
view to reaching some agreement with S.M.C.

At 1.30 p.m. even date the arrested man telephoned
to his shop and informed the manager that the Ta Tao
Police demanded the payment of $86.40, of which $19.20
represented the tax and the balance being fine for
refusal to pay the same.

At 2.40 p.m. even date, acting on instructions of
D.O. "J", the undersigned accompanied by S.I. Yamagouchi
again visited Mr. Kitaoka and the latter stated he had
had no time to deal with this case, but assured that the
arrested man would be released before 6 p.m.

At about 4 p.m. on the same date the arrested man
again telephoned to his shop requesting to make the
payment as soon as possible and stating that he would
not be released otherwise.

S.I. Yamaguchi and the undersigned again visited

that Sung Young Hang had been arrested not only for

当日下午1时30分，被捕者打电话到其店铺，告知经理大道警察要求支付86.40美元，其中19.20美元为税款，其余部分为因拒绝缴纳税款而处以的罚款。

当日下午2时40分，根据“J”区警官的指示，本人由山口巡查陪同再次拜访北冈先生，后者称他无暇处理此案，但保证在下午6点前释放被捕者。

同日约下午4时，被捕者再次致电其店铺，要求尽快付款，并称否则将不予释放。

当日下午4时30分，山口巡查和本人再次拜访北冈先生，获悉宋永航（音译）被捕不仅是因为

Ta Mei Pro and other local newspapers : 2 JULY 1938

COLLECTION OF MUNICIPAL RATE ON JESSFIELD ROAD

Jessfield Road is an extra-Settlement road.
Formerly the municipal rate in the district was collected
by the Shanghai City Government. The place has now
become a base of activities of lawless elements. Whenever
the Settlement police have occasion to make enquiries
about robberies or to make arrests of robbers in the
district, they are interfered with by Japanese gendarmes.
This state of affairs has created much anxiety among
residents in the outlying roads, which are, however,
supplied with electricity and water by the Shanghai
Waterworks Company and the Shanghai Power Company in the
International Settlement.
On June 28 the S.M.C. detailed Foreign
Sergeant No.127 and several tax collectors and Chinese
police constables to Mei Tsung Terrace (杨村), Jessfield
Road, to collect the municipal rate. A quarrel took
place between them and one of the tenants of the alleyway
named Yui Ya-yung (于重云). On the following day,
the foreign sergeant, in company with several tax
collectors, called at a foreign style tailor shop owned
by one Shih (石), which is located at the entrance of
the alleyway. Shortly afterwards a number of police
officers of the Shanghai Municipal Administration arrived
and prevented the Settlement officials from collecting
the rate. Fortunately no untoward incident took place.
It is learned that the residents on the
outlying districts are about to hold a meeting to discuss
the payment of the municipal rate.

（批：St C.）

杰斯菲尔德路市政捐税的征收

杰斯菲尔德路是一条越界筑路。以前该地区的市政捐税由上海市政府征收。此地现已成为不法分子的 activity 基地。每当租界警察在该地区查询抢劫案或逮捕劫匪时，都会受到日本宪兵的干涉。这种状况引起了外围道路居民的极大焦虑，然而这些道路由国际租界内的上海自来水公司和上海电力公司供应水电。
6月28日，工部局派遣外籍巡长第127号及数名收税员和华捕前往杰斯菲尔德路梅宗台（杨村）征收市政捐税。他们与弄堂内一名名为于重云的租户发生了争吵。次日，该外籍巡长会同几名收税员造访位于弄堂口的一家由石姓人士拥有的西式裁缝店。不久，多名上海市公安局警察赶到，阻止租界官员征收捐税。幸未发生不幸事件。
据悉，外围地区的居民正准备举行会议，讨论缴纳市政捐税事宜。

INTERFERENCE IN
S. M. COUNCIL TAX
COLLECTION SEEN

The collection of municipal rates
and "police tax" by collectors of
the S.M.C. in the extra-Settlement
areas is expected to be blocked by
police of the "Ta Tao Government"
in view of the latter's desire to
monopolise the collection, it was
reported in Chinese circles today.

Questioned by the Echo today
on the matter, Mr. Stirling-
Fessenden, Secretary-General of
the S.M.C., declared, "We will do
the best we can," and went on to
emphasize that "we shall stick to
the stand we have always taken,"
regarding the extra-Settlement
municipal rates.

However, in view of the grave
apprehension felt generally by
local Chinese inhabitants, not many
of them have so far returned to
the extra-Settlement areas to take
up their residence so that it is not
expected that there will be much
to the coveted "pie," local Chinese
circles believed.

Municipal rates for the quarter
ending September 30, 1938, were

《晚声报》

观察到大道政府干预
工部局税务征收

据今日华人圈子报道，鉴于大道政府希望垄断征收工作，工部局收税员在越界筑路区域征收市政捐税和“警察税”预计将受到“大道政府”警察的阻挠。

《晚声报》今日就此事项询问工部局总办史特灵·费森登先生，他宣称：“我们将尽力而为”，并继续强调，“关于越界筑路的市政捐税，我们将坚持我们一贯采取的立场。”

然而，鉴于当地中国居民普遍感到严重忧虑，迄今为止返回越界筑路区域居住的人并不多，因此当地华人圈子认为，这块令人垂涎的“蛋糕”并没有多少可分。

截至1938年9月30日的季度市政捐税，从昨日7月1日起应向工部局缴纳。

1.

Re. payment of taxes at 52 Jessfield Road, O.O.L.

Miss Maud T. Henderson, an American missionary, who lives at and superintends the St. Faith's Settlement, 52 Jessfield Road, telephoned Bubbling Well Station on 25/6/38, asking for advice regarding payment of taxes.

D.S. Greenfield visited Miss Henderson at her home. She stated:-

On 21/6/38, a Chinese purporting to be an official of the "Ta Tao Government", called on her and made enquiries as to whether her premises were equipped with electric light and telephone, and if she paid taxes to the Shanghai Municipal Council. When she informed him that electric light and telephone were installed, and that she paid S.M.C. taxes, the official handed her a tax paper to fill in, and instructed her that in future she was not to pay taxes to the S.M.C., but to the "Ta Tao Government."

Miss Henderson wrote to the American Consul regarding the visit of this person, and enclosed the paper she was given to complete. The American Consul has replied that as she is an S.M.C. taxpayer, he sees no reason why she should pay tax to an unrecognised government. The letter concludes, that should there be any further trouble, the matter should be brought to the attention of the Settlement Police.

关于杰斯菲尔德路52号外带酒牌的纳税事宜。

莫德·T·亨德森小姐，一位美国传教士，居住在杰斯菲尔德路52号的圣费思定居点并负责管理该处，于1938年6月25日致电静安寺警署，就纳税事宜寻求建议。

格林菲尔德侦探巡长前往亨德森小姐家中拜访。她陈述如下：

1938年6月21日，一名自称是“大道政府”官员的中国人拜访了她，询问她的房产是否配备电灯和电话，以及她是否向上海公共租界工部局纳税。当她告知对方已安装电灯和电话，且她向工部局纳税时，该官员递给她一张税单填写，并指示她今后不要向工部局纳税，而是向“大道政府”纳税。

亨德森小姐就此人来访一事致信美国领事，并附上了发给她的待填表格。美国领事回复称，鉴于她是工部局纳税人，他认为没有理由让她向一个未被承认的政府纳税。信的结尾指出，若再有麻烦，应将此事提请租界警察注意。

AMERICAN CONSULATE GENERAL
Shanghai, June 23, 1938.

Miss Maud T. Henderson,
St. Faith's Settlement,
52 Jessfield Road,
Shanghai.

Madam:

The receipt is acknowledged of your letter of
June 22, 1938, stating that you have been notified to
pay a property tax to the "Ta Tao Government" of
Shanghai. You enclose with your letter the form to
be filled out in connection with the payment of this
tax, and request the advice of this Consulate as to
the action which you should take.

Inasmuch as you are now, and have been for some
time, paying your house tax to the Shanghai Municipal
Council, there would seem to be no reason for you to
pay the house tax now being demanded by an unrecognized
government. It would seem to be in order for you to so
inform the tax collector should he call upon you again.
If he continues to trouble you with the matter it is
suggested that you bring the matter to the attention of
the Settlement police.

Very truly yours,
For the Consul General:

(Sgd.) J. Hall Paxton
American Consul.
